6:1.sourceText: Ἐν δὲ ταῖς ἡμέραις ταύταις πληθυνόντων τῶν μαθητῶν ἐγένετο γογγυσμὸς τῶν Ἑλληνιστῶν πρὸς τοὺς Ἑβραίους, ὅτι παρεθεωροῦντο ἐν τῇ διακονίᾳ τῇ καθημερινῇ αἱ χῆραι αὐτῶν.
6:1.targetText: And in these days, the disciples multiplying, there came a murmuring of the Hellenists at the Hebrews, because their widows were being overlooked in the daily ministry,

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles are not separately expressed with these days, the repeated daily qualifier, or their widows.

6:2.sourceText: προσκαλεσάμενοι δὲ οἱ δώδεκα τὸ πλῆθος τῶν μαθητῶν εἶπαν Οὐκ ἀρεστόν ἐστιν ἡμᾶς καταλείψαντας τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ διακονεῖν τραπέζαις.
6:2.targetText: and the Twelve, having called near the multitude of the disciples, said, “It is not pleasing that we, having left the word of God, minister at tables;

groups.note: Actual ἡμᾶς is the accusative personal subject of the ministering infinitive. English makes that same subject a finite that-we clause; no nominative Greek we pronoun or separate ὅτι is printed.
Actual διακονεῖν is an infinitive under not pleasing. English makes its that-we clause finite with minister, preserving the real infinitive head.
Actual dative tables gives the served-table relation, rendered at tables without a separately printed Greek at preposition.

6:3.sourceText: ἐπισκέψασθε δέ, ἀδελφοί, ἄνδρας ἐξ ὑμῶν μαρτυρουμένους ἑπτὰ πλήρεις Πνεύματος καὶ σοφίας, οὓς καταστήσομεν ἐπὶ τῆς χρείας ταύτης·
6:3.targetText: look out, therefore, brothers, seven men of you who are testified well of, full of the Holy Spirit and wisdom, whom we may set over this necessity,

groups.note: Actual μαρτυρουμένους is a present passive being-attested participle. LSV who are testified well of verbalizes that same attested-status modifier; no separate Greek well adverb or relative pronoun is printed.

Actual καταστήσομεν is future active indicative we will set/appoint. LSV uses we may set for that appointment predicate; the pinned CrossWire TR also records the future form here. The shared head retains the actual future analysis without a claimed Greek subjunctive or a different printed reading.

unmappedSource.reason: N1904 prints connective δέ. LSV follows the TR οὖν therefore reading; the distinct actual connectors remain explicit.
The Greek article is not separately expressed with this necessity.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV follows the TR οὖν connector while pinned N1904 has δέ, not a separately written therefore particle.
LSV includes Holy with Spirit, corroborated by TR ἁγίου. Pinned N1904 has the Spirit noun without that adjective here.

6:4.sourceText: ἡμεῖς δὲ τῇ προσευχῇ καὶ τῇ διακονίᾳ τοῦ λόγου προσκαρτερήσομεν.
6:4.targetText: and we to prayer, and to the ministry of the word, will give ourselves continually.”

groups.note: The actual dative article/prayer construction gives the activity attended to, rendered to prayer; the case-bearing article remains with its real prayer head.

Actual προσκαρτερήσομεν is the future continuing/persisting-in verb. English will give ourselves continually expresses that same sustained-attention predicate; no separate giving verb or reflexive pronoun is printed.

6:5.sourceText: καὶ ἤρεσεν ὁ λόγος ἐνώπιον παντὸς τοῦ πλήθους, καὶ ἐξελέξαντο Στέφανον, ἄνδρα πλήρη πίστεως καὶ Πνεύματος Ἁγίου, καὶ Φίλιππον καὶ Πρόχορον καὶ Νικάνορα καὶ Τίμωνα καὶ Παρμενᾶν καὶ Νικόλαον προσήλυτον Ἀντιοχέα,
6:5.targetText: And the thing was pleasing before all the multitude, and they chose Stephen, a man full of faith and the Holy Spirit, and Philip, and Prochorus, and Nicanor, and Timon, and Parmenas, and Nicolaus, a proselyte of Antioch,

groups.note: Actual λόγος is the saying/statement noun, rendered thing for the stated proposal; the source remains λόγος rather than a substituted πρᾶγμα thing noun.
Actual Ἀντιοχέα is the Antiochene personal adjective, rendered of Antioch; no separate source Antioch place noun or of preposition is printed.

6:6.sourceText: οὓς ἔστησαν ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀποστόλων, καὶ προσευξάμενοι ἐπέθηκαν αὐτοῖς τὰς χεῖρας.
6:6.targetText: whom they set before the apostles, and they, having prayed, laid [their] hands on them.

groups.note: The actual definite hands are the body part of those performing the laying-on action. English [their] hands makes that subject-owned bodily relation explicit; the real article/hands construction remains the source without an invented separate personal possessive.

6:7.sourceText: Καὶ ὁ λόγος τοῦ Θεοῦ ηὔξανεν, καὶ ἐπληθύνετο ὁ ἀριθμὸς τῶν μαθητῶν ἐν Ἱερουσαλὴμ σφόδρα, πολύς τε ὄχλος τῶν ἱερέων ὑπήκουον τῇ πίστει.
6:7.targetText: And the word of God increased, and the number of the disciples multiplied in Jerusalem exceedingly; a great multitude of the priests were also obedient to the faith.

groups.note: Actual ὑπήκουον is imperfect obeyed/were-obeying. LSV were obedient expresses the same verbal obedience predicate with adjective-plus-copula wording, not a separately written Greek adjective and be verb.

6:8.sourceText: Στέφανος δὲ πλήρης χάριτος καὶ δυνάμεως ἐποίει τέρατα καὶ σημεῖα μεγάλα ἐν τῷ λαῷ.
6:8.targetText: And Stephen, full of faith and power, was doing great wonders and signs among the people,

unmappedSource.reason: N1904 prints χάριτος, grace, as the first fullness content. LSV follows the different TR πίστεως faith reading; the real grace and faith heads remain separate.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV follows TR πίστεως faith as the fullness content. Pinned N1904 prints χάριτος grace, without an actual faith noun in this verse.

6:9.sourceText: ἀνέστησαν δέ τινες τῶν ἐκ τῆς συναγωγῆς τῆς λεγομένης Λιβερτίνων καὶ Κυρηναίων καὶ Ἀλεξανδρέων καὶ τῶν ἀπὸ Κιλικίας καὶ Ἀσίας συνζητοῦντες τῷ Στεφάνῳ,
6:9.targetText: and there arose certain of those of the synagogue, the [one] called Libertines (and Cyrenians, and Alexandrians, and of those from Cilicia, and Asia), disputing with Stephen,

groups.note: The actual dative article/Stephen phrase is the disputing counterpart, rendered with Stephen. The real personal head and case relation remain one construction without an independent Greek with preposition.

6:10.sourceText: καὶ οὐκ ἴσχυον ἀντιστῆναι τῇ σοφίᾳ καὶ τῷ Πνεύματι ᾧ ἐλάλει.
6:10.targetText: and they were not able to resist the wisdom and the Spirit with which he was speaking;

groups.note: Actual dative relative ᾧ supplies the speaking means, rendered with which without a separately printed Greek with preposition.

6:11.sourceText: τότε ὑπέβαλον ἄνδρας λέγοντας ὅτι Ἀκηκόαμεν αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος ῥήματα βλάσφημα εἰς Μωϋσῆν καὶ τὸν Θεόν·
6:11.targetText: then they suborned men, saying, “We have heard him speaking slanderous sayings in regard to Moses and God.”

unmappedSource.reason: Greek ὅτι introduces the quotation. English uses direct quotation without a separate that word.
The Greek article is not separately expressed with God.

6:12.sourceText: συνεκίνησάν τε τὸν λαὸν καὶ τοὺς πρεσβυτέρους καὶ τοὺς γραμματεῖς, καὶ ἐπιστάντες συνήρπασαν αὐτὸν καὶ ἤγαγον εἰς τὸ συνέδριον,
6:12.targetText: They also stirred up the people, and the elders, and the scribes, and having come on [him], they caught him, and brought [him] to the Sanhedrin;

groups.note: The one actual personal seizure-object is the same patient of the immediate coming-on, catching, and bringing sequence. English states [him], him, and [him] across those local acts; all retain one real source identity.

6:13.sourceText: ἔστησάν τε μάρτυρας ψευδεῖς λέγοντας Ὁ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος οὐ παύεται λαλῶν ῥήματα κατὰ τοῦ τόπου τοῦ ἁγίου καὶ τοῦ νόμου·
6:13.targetText: they also set up false witnesses, saying, “This one does not cease to speak evil sayings against this holy place and the Law,

groups.note: The actual article/man/this constituent is rendered This one, a generic personal designation of the same named man; no independently printed Greek one numeral is substituted.
Actual λαλῶν is a present speaking participle selected with cease. English to speak recasts that same continuing activity as an infinitive; the printed Greek participial form remains.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles with the holy place are not separately expressed by English this holy place.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV includes an evil/slanderous qualifier with sayings, corroborated by TR βλάσφημα, absent from pinned N1904 here.
LSV includes the place demonstrative, corroborated by TR τούτου. Pinned N1904 has the definite holy-place construction without that separate demonstrative.

6:14.sourceText: ἀκηκόαμεν γὰρ αὐτοῦ λέγοντος ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ὁ Ναζωραῖος οὗτος καταλύσει τὸν τόπον τοῦτον καὶ ἀλλάξει τὰ ἔθη ἃ παρέδωκεν ἡμῖν Μωϋσῆς.
6:14.targetText: for we have heard him saying that this Jesus the Nazarean will overthrow this place, and will change the customs that Moses delivered to us”;

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with this place.

6:15.sourceText: καὶ ἀτενίσαντες εἰς αὐτὸν πάντες οἱ καθεζόμενοι ἐν τῷ συνεδρίῳ εἶδον τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ ὡσεὶ πρόσωπον ἀγγέλου.
6:15.targetText: and gazing at him, all those sitting in the Sanhedrin saw his face as it were the face of a messenger.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with his face.
